findings.title: The new per-ID delete can exceed supported parameter counts on non-SQLite databases
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` creates one bound parameter for every selected ID except for SQLite. `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configurable and the added test explicitly exercises 32,767 IDs; this exceeds SQL Server's 2,100-parameter limit (and sufficiently large configured values can exceed limits on other supported dialects). The previous DELETE used no per-ID bind list, so such configurations worked. On those deployments cleanup will fail each batch and old annotations/tags will accumulate. Split the delete into dialect-safe chunks or apply the same safe literal/chunking strategy for every dialect with a parameter limit.

findings.title: Cleanup scheduling is changed from every ten minutes to every minute for all cleanup jobs
findings.body: This unrelated change makes the entire cleanup suite run ten times as often, not just annotation cleanup. It increases database scans/deletes and filesystem work for snapshots, dashboard versions, images, short URLs, query history, and annotations, and can cause a long-running cleanup to be re-run immediately after it completes because the ticker has already fired. There is no corresponding configuration or PR rationale for this broad scheduling change; retain the ten-minute interval unless this load increase is explicitly intended and validated.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors and dump every selected ID
findings.body: Every batch logs at Error level before and after deletion even when `err` is nil, and includes the complete `ids` slice. A configured large batch (the added test uses 32,767 IDs) produces very large error log entries for normal operation, pollutes error monitoring, and can materially increase logging/storage load during cleanup. Log only actual errors at Error level and use a non-error level with counts rather than the full ID list for successful batches.
